readings: Take the average transaction count per account over only the accounts that have at least one financial transaction. Compute that average over all such accounts, before dropping any accounts for a missing customer or town. Then show the 10 accounts with the highest ratio of their transaction count to that average, highest first. For each, give the account id, the town_city of the customer holding it, its number of transactions, its share of the total transactions made by accounts in that town, and the ratio to the average. Exclude accounts whose customer isn't in Customers or has a null/empty town_city. Do not round.

Take the average transaction count per account over every account in the Accounts table, counting accounts with no transactions as 0. Compute that average before dropping any accounts for a missing customer or town. Then show the 10 accounts with the highest ratio of their transaction count to that average, highest first. For each, give the account id, the town_city of the customer holding it, its number of transactions, its share of the total transactions made by accounts in that town, and the ratio to the average. Exclude accounts whose customer isn't in Customers or has a null/empty town_city. Do not round.

First restrict to accounts that have at least one financial transaction and whose holder exists in Customers with a non-null town_city. Compute the average transaction count per account over only those accounts. Then show the 10 accounts with the highest ratio of their transaction count to that average, highest first. For each, give the account id, the town_city of the customer holding it, its number of transactions, its share of the total transactions made by accounts in that town, and the ratio to the average. Do not round.
queries:
WITH acct AS (
  SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM Financial_Transactions
  GROUP BY account_id
),
avg_all AS (
  SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS avg_cnt FROM acct
),
joined AS (
  SELECT a.account_id, c.town_city, acct.cnt
  FROM acct
  JOIN Accounts a ON a.account_id = acct.account_id
  JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = a.customer_id
  WHERE c.town_city IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(c.town_city) <> ''
)
SELECT j.account_id,
       j.town_city,
       j.cnt AS transaction_count,
       j.cnt * 1.0 / SUM(j.cnt) OVER (PARTITION BY j.town_city) AS share_of_town,
       j.cnt * 1.0 / (SELECT avg_cnt FROM avg_all) AS ratio_to_average
FROM joined j
ORDER BY ratio_to_average DESC
LIMIT 10;
WITH tc AS (
  SELECT a.account_id, a.customer_id, COUNT(ft.transaction_id) AS cnt
  FROM Accounts a
  LEFT JOIN Financial_Transactions ft ON ft.account_id = a.account_id
  GROUP BY a.account_id, a.customer_id
),
avg_all AS (
  SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS avg_cnt FROM tc
),
valid AS (
  SELECT tc.account_id, c.town_city, tc.cnt
  FROM tc
  JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = tc.customer_id
  WHERE c.town_city IS NOT NULL AND c.town_city <> ''
)
SELECT v.account_id,
       v.town_city,
       v.cnt AS transaction_count,
       v.cnt * 1.0 / SUM(v.cnt) OVER (PARTITION BY v.town_city) AS share_of_town_transactions,
       v.cnt / (SELECT avg_cnt FROM avg_all) AS ratio_to_average
FROM valid v
ORDER BY ratio_to_average DESC
LIMIT 10;
WITH acct AS (
  SELECT a.account_id, c.town_city, COUNT(*) AS n
  FROM Accounts a
  JOIN Customers c ON a.customer_id = c.customer_id
  JOIN Financial_Transactions t ON t.account_id = a.account_id
  WHERE c.town_city IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY a.account_id, c.town_city
),
avgt AS (
  SELECT AVG(n) * 1.0 AS avg_n FROM acct
)
SELECT
  acct.account_id,
  acct.town_city,
  acct.n AS num_transactions,
  acct.n * 1.0 / SUM(acct.n) OVER (PARTITION BY acct.town_city) AS town_share,
  acct.n / avgt.avg_n AS ratio_to_average
FROM acct, avgt
ORDER BY ratio_to_average DESC, acct.account_id
LIMIT 10;
